angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 452,205 km at 28.54 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 35.0395 +/- 0.0143 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 28.54 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.65 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 452,205 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.64 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4072 +/- 121 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2427 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2427.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.618, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
